<cite ref="Bava Metzia 103a:8">B. Mets. 103ᵃ</cite> if a person says, lend me thy hoe <he>למירפק ביה האי פ׳ … ההוא פ׳</he> to dig up this garden with it, he is allowed to use it for that garden only; <he>פ׳ … כל פ׳ וכ׳</he> if he says, ‘a garden’, he may use it for any garden he chooses.—Pl. <cite ref="Q00958"><he>פַּרְדֵּסִין</he></cite>, <he>פַּרְדְּסַיָּא</he>; <cite ref="Q01579"><he>פַּרְדֵּי׳</he></cite>, <cite ref="Q01579"><he>פַּרְדֵּיסֵי</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Judges 4:5">Targ. Jud. IV, 5</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Genesis 14:10">Targ. Y. Gen. XIV, 10</cite> (h. text <he>השדים</he>).

<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Ecclesiastes 2:5">Targ. Koh. II, 5</cite>; a. e.—B. Mets. l. c. <he>פ׳ רפיק ואזיל כל פ׳ וכ׳</he> if he says, ‘to dig up gardens’, he may use it for all the gardens he has.
